description: An action currently available on a media buy, resolved against the buy's current status, accepted commercial_terms.change_terms, account authorization, and applicable governance delegation. Authoritative for current availability, but not a replacement for negotiated rights: when explicit change_terms exist, this projection may temporarily omit an action because state changed, but MUST NOT silently replace its negotiated service mode, SLA, constraints, conditions, or contract reference. The containing array is uniquely keyed by action.

anyOf.description: Actions the buyer can perform on a media buy. Used as the action identifier in both the legacy flat `valid_actions[]` field (string array) and the structured `available_actions[]` field on buy responses, and in `allowed_actions[]` on Product. The coarse values (`update_budget`, `update_dates`, `update_packages`, `sync_creatives`) predate the finer-grained vocabulary and are retained for backwards compatibility — see `x-deprecated-enum-values`. Sellers SHOULD declare the finer-grained values where their platform distinguishes them; the coarse values roll up to the finer set per `enumMetadata[<value>].rollup`. See action-to-field mapping table in docs/media-buy/task-reference/update_media_buy.mdx for the normative binding between each action and the fields it covers on update_media_buy.

enumDescriptions.add_packages: Add new packages to an existing media buy via `new_packages` on update_media_buy.
enumDescriptions.cancel: Cancel the media buy. Irreversible. Maps to `canceled: true` on update_media_buy.
enumDescriptions.decrease_budget: Lower the media-buy total budget or one or more package caps. Maps to a lower `total_budget.amount` or lower values on `packages[].budget`. Sellers typically bound this by already-spent.
enumDescriptions.extend_flight: Push the buy's `end_time` later. Start time unchanged.
enumDescriptions.increase_budget: Raise the media-buy total budget, raise one or more package caps, or remove a seller-optimized package cap. Maps to a higher `total_budget.amount`, higher values on `packages[].budget`, or `packages[].budget: null` (which relaxes the ceiling).
enumDescriptions.pause: Pause the entire media buy. Maps to `paused: true` on update_media_buy.
enumDescriptions.reallocate_budget: Redistribute budget across packages on `packages[].budget` without changing the sum.
enumDescriptions.remove_creative: Remove a creative from the buy. Often the most time-sensitive action when a creative misbehaves; sellers SHOULD support self_serve removal where possible even when add/swap require approval.
enumDescriptions.remove_packages: Remove packages from a media buy.
enumDescriptions.replace_creative: Swap a creative for another without changing assignment logic. Distinct AM workflow from changing the assignment set.
enumDescriptions.resume: Resume a paused media buy. Maps to `paused: false` on update_media_buy.
enumDescriptions.shorten_flight: Pull the buy's `end_time` earlier. Start time unchanged.
enumDescriptions.sync_creatives: Coarse legacy action covering any creative-related change. Retained for backwards compatibility with 3.x sellers that emit this rather than the finer `replace_creative`/`update_creative_assignments`/`remove_creative`. Removed in 4.0. Sellers SHOULD migrate to the finer vocabulary.
enumDescriptions.update_bidding: Replace or clear the media-buy bidding default or package-authored bidding overrides. Maps to `bidding` and `packages[].bidding`; the seller validates the resulting effective policies atomically before mutation.
enumDescriptions.update_budget: Coarse legacy action covering any budget change. Retained for backwards compatibility with 3.x sellers that emit this rather than the finer `increase_budget`/`decrease_budget`/`reallocate_budget`. Removed in 4.0. Sellers SHOULD migrate to the finer vocabulary.
enumDescriptions.update_budget_allocation: Change fixed versus seller-optimized allocation mode, cross-package optimization goals, or package minimum-spend targets. Maps to `budget_allocation` and `packages[].min_spend_target`, including null to clear a target. Automatic seller allocation within an already-authorized seller-optimized buy is delivery behavior, not this action.
enumDescriptions.update_creative_assignments: Change which creatives are assigned to which packages.
enumDescriptions.update_dates: Coarse legacy action covering any flight-date change. Retained for backwards compatibility with 3.x sellers that emit this rather than the finer `extend_flight`/`shorten_flight`/`update_flight_dates`. Removed in 4.0. Sellers SHOULD migrate to the finer vocabulary.
enumDescriptions.update_flight_dates: Shift `start_time` and/or `end_time`. Distinct from extend/shorten because shifting a start date is operationally different from extending an end date and approval paths typically differ.
enumDescriptions.update_name: Replace the human-readable media-buy name without changing accepted commercial terms. Maps to `name` on update_media_buy or control_media_buy.
enumDescriptions.update_pacing: Update aggregate media-buy pacing or pacing on existing packages.
enumDescriptions.update_packages: Coarse legacy action covering any package update. Retained for backwards compatibility with 3.x sellers that emit this rather than the finer `update_targeting`/`update_pacing`/`update_frequency_caps`/`reallocate_budget`/`remove_packages`. Removed in 4.0. Sellers SHOULD migrate to the finer vocabulary.
enumDescriptions.update_targeting: Update targeting overlays on existing packages.

enumMetadata.$comment: Structured per-action metadata. Each entry carries `update_fields` (the `update_media_buy` request fields this action covers, as dotted paths rooted at the request body) and optional `rollup` for legacy coarse values that are superseded by finer-grained vocabulary. SDKs MUST consume this block to dispatch update_media_buy requests rather than parsing the field-mapping table in the update_media_buy task-reference doc; the doc is the human-readable mirror of this normative data. Deprecated values are marked at the top-level `x-deprecated-enum-values` (repo convention); SDKs and codegen MAY hide deprecated values from caller-facing surfaces when any value in the entry's `rollup` array is present in the same `available_actions[]` or `valid_actions[]` payload. Structured-only actions that are absent from this deprecated flat enum, such as update_media_buy_frequency_cap, carry the same enumMetadata shape in core/media-buy-available-action-id.json; SDKs MUST merge both blocks.

anyOf.title: Media Buy Valid Action
anyOf.x-deprecated-enum-values-doc: Coarse legacy values retained for backwards compatibility with 3.x sellers. Each rolls up to one or more finer-grained values published in 3.1 (see `enumMetadata[<value>].rollup`). Removed in 4.0.

applicable_package_ids.description: For a package-scoped action, the exact packages currently eligible. Omission means every relevant package. Root actions omit this field.

items.description: A package identifier to which a package-scoped media-buy action currently applies.
items.title: Applicable Package ID

change_term_id.description: The accepted proposal change_terms[].term_id from which this current-state action projection was derived.
change_term_id.title: Media Buy Change Term ID

mode.description: The single mode that applies right now on this buy for this action. Singular because the buy has a concrete state, exactly one mode applies. Buyer SDKs branch on this to decide whether to expect a synchronous response, conditional handling, or an asynchronous approval callback.

enumDescriptions.conditional_self_serve: Seller completes the action automatically within declared tolerances and uses seller-managed processing outside them. Constraint metadata defining the tolerances is out of scope for v1; buyers cannot statically predict which path will apply unless negotiated terms define it.
enumDescriptions.requires_approval: Legacy 3.x mode indicating an approval-dependent async path. New declarations SHOULD use seller_managed so the protocol describes externally meaningful processing without exposing internal workflow.
enumDescriptions.self_serve: Seller honors the request synchronously without approval or conditional checks. Buyer SDKs dispatch the task declared on the available action; legacy entries without task metadata use update_media_buy.
enumDescriptions.seller_managed: Asynchronous seller-managed processing. Buyer SDKs use the standard submitted, working, and input-required lifecycle and do not infer whether a person, model, queue, or other internal control is involved.

mode.title: Media Buy Action Mode

sla.description: Optional SLA commitment for this action on this buy. Absence means no commitment, not zero commitment.

completion_max.description: Maximum elapsed time from buyer issuing the action to the seller completing it (mutation applied, proposal finalized, or seller-managed decision resolved). Sellers include weekends and non-working periods in the maximum. ISO 8601 duration.

response_max.description: Maximum elapsed time from when the buyer issues the action to when the seller acknowledges receipt (mode-appropriate: synchronous response for self_serve, tolerance decision for conditional_self_serve, or queue acknowledgement for seller_managed and legacy requires_approval). Sellers include weekends and non-working periods in the maximum. ISO 8601 duration.

sla.title: SLA Window

task.description: Compact-lifecycle task for this resolved action: operational control, commercial refinement, or creative lifecycle mutation.

terms_ref.description: Deprecated 3.1 opaque commercial-terms pointer. A 3.2 compatibility projection MAY echo change_term_id here for older buyers, but new buyers MUST prefer change_term_id and MUST NOT assume an arbitrary 3.1 value identifies an accepted change term.
terms_ref.title: Media Buy Terms Reference

title: Media Buy Available Action

verifier_constraints.applicable_package_scope: Every applicable_package_ids value identifies a package of this media buy.
verifier_constraints.change_term_link: When change_term_id is present, it resolves to exactly one accepted_proposal.commercial_terms.change_terms[].term_id whose action, service_mode, and processing_sla agree with this projection.
verifier_constraints.legacy_alias_agreement: When change_term_id and deprecated terms_ref are both present and terms_ref is being used as the proposal-term link, their values are identical. A 3.1 terms_ref with no accepted change term remains an opaque legacy commercial pointer and MUST NOT be reinterpreted as authority.
